war_declared.text: The council has spoken. {my_faction} will answer {enemy_faction} in the field. I did say patience had a price.
{enemy_faction} chose the sword over the ledger. Pity. The ledger was so much more civil for everyone involved.
Blood is spilt where letters have failed, and I wrote a great many letters. Good luck to {my_faction}, I suspect.
Every councillor of {my_faction} voted for this war. Those who abstained, I shall remember with great care.

peace_made.text: The treaty with {faction} is sealed at last. {my_faction} may breathe, though the lords will sulk all season.
Peace with {faction}, bought over three long dinners and one dreadful wine. Worth every course, I suspect.
{my_faction} and {faction} shake hands today. Do not mistake a truce for trust, friends. I certainly do not.
Terms agreed with {faction}. I drafted the clauses myself, so do read the small print before you celebrate.
The war with {faction} is over, and I was there for every letter that ended it. Few will say so, of course.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. A sensible choice, and one I may have encouraged quietly over tea.
Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Do tell me later what made you choose us over the others.
{player}, you have joined {my_faction} after all. I shall pretend not to notice the look on your face when you did.
{my_faction} gains {player}, and the council gains a clever mind. I have said so in every letter this week.
You are now of {my_faction}, {player}. Mind the minutes of the next assembly. They matter more than the banners.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has gone over to {faction}, and {my_faction} is poorer for it. I shall not say I am surprised.
{player}, you left {my_faction} for {faction}. A bold choice. I do hope the new benches are comfortable.
{player} abandons {my_faction} for {faction}. Such things happen when the council forgets to listen.
{player}, I understand the move to {faction}. Do keep your old letters, in case you ever wish to return.
Several of {my_faction} will call {player}'s move a betrayal. I call it a lesson in where the real power sits.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} now belongs to {player}. Well earned, though I did draft the petition that made it possible, you understand.
So {fief} is yours, {player}. Enjoy the rents. I shall keep an eye on the ledgers, as all good councillors do.
{player} receives {fief} while others wait years for a hearing. How remarkable the council's memory has become.
{fief}, {player}? I wrote the petition for that seat myself. Still, I suppose the council owes you something.
Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Ruling a town means a great many letters. I can recommend a clerk or two.

whisper_alliance_offer.text: {player}, {rival} has been spending {enemy_faction}'s gold quietly. Shall the two of us make better use of it?
{player}, I have no wish to share a table with {rival}. Yet we both hold little love for {enemy_faction}.
{player}, consider a pact against {enemy_faction}. {rival} would be left with very little to bargain with.
Let us speak plainly, {player}. {enemy_faction} stands between us and better fiefs, and {rival} stands in the way.
{player}, between us, {rival} has been writing to {enemy_faction}. I would rather we answered those letters first.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} has fallen to {my_faction} at last. {enemy_faction} will want it back, and I intend to make them argue for it.
The banners of {my_faction} now fly over {fief}. A quiet siege, and a considerably louder council vote.
{fief} was taken from {enemy_faction} this week. The council will hear the details from me first, naturally.
Well done to {my_faction}. {fief} is ours, and {enemy_faction} will be reading the terms of surrender with great interest.

player_took_my_fief.text: {player} has taken {fief} from us. Enjoy the walls, {player}. Walls have a way of becoming expensive.
{player}, {fief} was mine to lose in council, not yours to take in the field. I will remember the difference.
{player} now holds {fief}. A bold move, and one I might have made myself had the vote gone differently.
{fief} is yours now, {player}. I bear no grudge, merely a long memory and a very good quill.
You took {fief} while the council was still deciding, {player}. Such timing is either brilliant or rude.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: {player}, I accept gladly. {rival} will soon discover the cost of trusting {enemy_faction} over us, I suspect.
Very well, {player}. Let us stand together against {enemy_faction}, and let {rival} wonder what we said.
A fine decision, {player}. Our parties will march together against {enemy_faction}, and {rival} can watch from the hill.
Agreed, {player}. We will set the terms down later, when our captains are not listening. Against {enemy_faction}, then.
{player}, you have my word. {rival} has been too comfortable for too long, and {enemy_faction} will not hold out forever.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, {player}. I would sooner share a table with {rival} than with you, and that is saying a great deal.
I must decline, {player}. Our captains have other engagements, and so does my patience. Another season, perhaps.
Not today, {player}, and I am sorry for it. Bring me proper terms and I will reconsider, you have my word.
{player}, your offer is generous only to yourself. {rival} made the same request last week and received no answer.
I suspect not, {player}. The council has not yet given its blessing, and I never move without it.

ambient_chatter.text: The rain over {town} has soaked every petition in the square. Half the council is sneezing through the vote.
Has anyone else heard that {village} wants a new reeve? I have several suggestions, all of them written down.
Fog on the road to {town} again. Good for ambushes, bad for anyone trying to reach the council on time.
The bread in {town} tastes better than the speeches in its hall. Do not quote me on that, I suspect.
Lag or not, the bell in {village} rang exactly when the council began. Someone's timing is impeccable.
